column20: REPORTING-BASIS BREAK, RESOLVED BY THE SOURCE ITSELF. Every edition through 2020-21 labels furnace oil 'Tonnes'; every edition from 2022-23 labels the same row 'Liters/thousand', and nothing announces the change. The 2023-24 edition settles it against itself: its p.163 detail table heads the column 'Furnace Oil (M. Tonnes)' and gives 15.083 locomotive plus 64.824 other, and the narrative on the same page states '79.907 M.T of furnace oil'. The Principal Statistics unit column is unreliable in that very table - it labels Persons Employed 'Tonne' and Cost of Employees 'No.'. So the basis is TONNES and the published_unit_label is simply wrong; the quantity is now carried as 79.907 tonnes rather than 80 thousand litres. The published_unit_label column preserves what each edition actually said so the break cannot be lost. It does not matter numerically - furnace oil is under 0.001 Mt CO2e on either reading, and tests/test_railways.py pins that - but it is exactly the kind of silent basis change that ruined the Sindh vehicle series in the transport sector, so it is recorded rather than smoothed.
